name: low_vol_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (Ang et al. 2006) — low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns than high-vol stocks — manifests intraday in Indian markets. NIFTY 50 stocks in the bottom tercile of 20-day realized vol that also show positive intraday momentum (price > VWAP, EMA alignment) outperform high-vol stocks with similar momentum characteristics. This is because low-vol stocks attract institutional accumulation (steady, predictable) while high-vol stocks attract speculative flow (noisy, mean-reverting). The strategy goes long low-vol momentum stocks and short high-vol momentum stocks, capturing the low-vol premium intraday.
stock_filter: rank stocks by 20-day realized vol; long bottom tercile, short top tercile (with momentum filter)
indicators: intraday_momentum = close > vwap AND EMA(close, 9) > EMA(close, 21)

conditions: low_vol == True (stock in bottom vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True (above VWAP, EMAs aligned up)
long.confirmation: close makes new session high while above VWAP

conditions: high_vol == True (stock in top vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True for short (below VWAP, EMAs aligned down)
short.confirmation: close makes new session low while below VWAP

entry.entry_price: market order; size long leg 1.2x short leg to account for beta difference

exit.target: long leg outperforms short leg by 30bps (relative target)
exit.stop_loss: long leg underperforms short leg by 25bps OR either leg hits 0.5% absolute loss
exit.trailing_stop: after 15bps relative outperformance, trail at 5bps relative
exit.time_stop: hold for session unless stopped out (this is a factor bet, not a quick trade)
exit.signal_exit: if VIX spikes > 20 during trade, close (vol regime shift breaks the anomaly)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; low-vol anomaly weakens in high-VIX environments (all stocks become high-vol)
filters.volume_filter: both long and short stocks must have avg volume > ₹100cr/day
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 2%); factor bets work in moderate markets
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings today; skip budget/RBI days
other_filters: rebalance vol ranking daily before market open; don't use stale rankings

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — low-vol anomaly is well-documented and may compress as more quant funds exploit it

weaknesses: The low-vol anomaly is primarily a cross-sectional effect over weeks/months; compressing it to intraday may not capture the same economic forces (institutional preference, leverage aversion)
Two-leg execution with stocks from different sectors creates idiosyncratic risk that may dominate the low-vol factor return on any given day
In risk-off environments (sharp selloffs), low-vol stocks also sell off, and the short high-vol leg may actually outperform (short squeeze), creating large losses
prior_art: Ang et al. (2006) cross-section of vol and returns; Baker et al. (2011) betting against beta; Blitz & Van Vliet (2007) low-vol effect. Intraday adaptation is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 35bps - 0.42 * 25bps = 20.3 - 10.5 = 9.8bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (two legs). Net negative per trade! The 22bps daily estimate relies on the full-session hold allowing the factor to express. Factor bets need time; this is borderline for intraday. Consider as supplementary only.
